  "text": "The woman at the allotment gate asked which plot was mine.

“Seventeen,” I said. “It was my mother's.”

She moved her wheelbarrow so I could get past.

“There's a key for the shed. Under the brick.”

I had brought bin bags and a pair of gloves. The council letter said I had until the end of the month to clear it.

Inside the shed were three spades, a folding chair and a calendar from the previous year. My mother had written planting dates in the squares. On a shelf stood a mug with teaspoons in it, all dark at one end.

I put the calendar in a bag.

The woman appeared at the door holding two courgettes.

“These are yours.”

“I don't really cook.”

“They'll keep a few days.”

She laid them on the chair and looked at the bags.

“Are you giving it up?”

“I work Saturdays.”

“You can come other days.”

From somewhere beyond the shed came the noise of a hose being dragged along a path.

“I wouldn't know what to do,” I said.

The woman pointed at a patch beside the door.

“Those onions can come up.”

I followed her outside. She loosened one with a fork, then passed the fork to me.

By noon I had filled half a bag. She told me to leave it open or they would sweat.

Before locking the shed, I took the calendar out of the rubbish. I hung it back on its nail, although the dates were no use now.

At the gate I asked the woman when she usually came."
